The center of mass of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ is given by 

$$
(\overset{―}{x},\overset{―}{y})=(\frac{{M}_{y}}{m},\frac{{M}_{x}}{m}),
$$

where 

- $m={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A$ is the mass of the lamina,

- ${M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A\,$ is the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis, and

- ${M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A$ is the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.

Notice that $D$ is a type II plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/78f9da3d48727d2cb3c447be0f4050a044c4aabe29179fd31f04cd7b6c66eabd.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1-{y}^{2},\,-1\le y\le 1}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)={y}^{2}.$ 

Since we require the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass, we need to compute the moment about the $y$-axis: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot {y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1-{y}^{2}}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}\cdot (1-2{y}^{2}+{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}-2{y}^{4}+{y}^{6}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}-2{y}^{4}+{y}^{6}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}-\frac{2}{5}{y}^{5}+\frac{1}{7}{y}^{7}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{7} \\  & =\frac{8}{105}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{y}}{m}=\frac{(\frac{8}{105})}{(\frac{4}{15})}=\frac{2}{7}.
$$
